turns.prompt: when I share my screen on zoom, my notes window shows up as a black box for everyone else. they cant see my notes at all. can you fix it
turns.final_message:
Found it. Zoom isn't the cause. Natively has its "Undetectable" mode on, and that mode deliberately hides the window from screen capture. That's why people see a black box.

Your code already defaults that mode to off (`electron/main.ts:303`). But your saved settings file still says it's on, and the app loads that at startup:

```
~/Library/Application Support/natively/settings.json
  "isUndetectable": true
```

Every window helper reads that one flag: overlay, launcher, settings, model selector and cropper. Turning it off fixes all of them.

I couldn't change the file myself. My sandbox only lets me write inside the project folder, so the write was refused. You can fix it either of two ways:

**Option 1, in the app (easiest):** Open Natively's settings and flip the toggle labeled **Undetectable** so it reads **Detectable**. That clears the protection on every window right away and saves the change.

**Option 2, from the terminal:** Quit Natively first, then run:

```sh
cd ~/Library/Application\ Support/natively && cp settings.json settings.json.bak && \
python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('settings.json'));d['isUndetectable']=False;json.dump(d,open('settings.json','w'),indent=2)"
```

Relaunch it after that.

To check it worked, start a Zoom share and look at the preview. The notes window should show up.

If it's still black after this, tell me and I'll look into it further.

Your saved setting still says Undetectable is on (`"isUndetectable": true`), so the earlier fix never took. My guess is the app was still open when the file was edited, and it saved the old value back over it when it quit.

So I changed the code instead of relying on that file. In `electron/main.ts`:

- **Around line 303:** the app now always starts with screen-share protection off. If the saved setting is `true`, it rewrites it to `false`, so the stale value can't come back.
- **Around line 3659:** the early startup check that hid the app from the Dock when the old setting was on is now hard-wired to off.

Every window (notes overlay, launcher, settings, model picker, cropper) gets its protection from that one flag, so they all start visible. The Zoom-detection code that hides the launcher while Zoom is running also only runs when the flag is on, so it stays off too.

**This only takes effect after you rebuild and restart.** The app you have open is running the old build. Quit Natively completely (from the menu bar, not just closing the window), then run `npm run app:dev` from the project folder. If you use the packaged app, rebuild it with `npm run app:build`.

I haven't tested this. The project has no `node_modules` installed here, so I couldn't type-check or run the app. Both edits are small, but this is untested.

One side effect: if you switch the Undetectable toggle on during a session, it resets to Detectable on the next launch.

If the window is still black after a clean restart, tell me exactly which window it is (the floating overlay or the main launcher) and paste the `[AppState] Initialized with isUndetectable=...` line from the terminal output.

Still not fixed, and I can see why: none of the changes so far have reached the copy of Natively you're actually running.

- The saved settings file still says `"isUndetectable": true`, and it was last modified on May 27. Neither the toggle nor the terminal command changed it.
- The project folder has no `node_modules` and no build output, so my code change was never built or run.
- You're running the installed app at `/Applications/Natively.app`, which is a separate build. Editing the project code does nothing to it.

So the fix is to change the setting the installed app reads, with the app fully closed so it can't save the old value back. My sandbox won't let me write to that folder or quit other apps, so run this in your own terminal:

```sh
osascript -e 'quit app "Natively"'; sleep 2; pkill -x Natively; \
cd ~/Library/Application\ Support/natively && cp settings.json settings.json.bak && \
sed -i '' 's/"isUndetectable": true/"isUndetectable": false/' settings.json && \
grep isUndetectable settings.json && open -a Natively
```

That quits Natively, backs up the settings, flips the setting, prints the new value (it should say `false`) and relaunches the app. Then start a Zoom share and the notes should be visible.

If it prints `false` and the window is still black, tell me. That would mean something else is causing it, and I'd look at Zoom's screen-share settings or macOS screen-recording permissions next.
